{{Short description|American molecular biologist and AIDS denialist}}
[[File:Harvey Bialy in Speaking Portraits.jpg|thumb|Harvey Bialy in Speaking Portraits]]
'''Harvey Bialy''' (born 1945, New York City) was an American [[molecular biology|molecular biologist]] and [[AIDS denialist]]. He was one of the signatories to a [[letter to the editor]] by the "Group for the Scientific Reappraisal of the HIV-AIDS Hypothesis", which denied that [[HIV]] was the cause of [[AIDS]],<ref>Epstein, Steven. ''Impure Science'', University of California Press, 1996. pp 143-144.</ref> and was a member of the controversial and heavily criticized South African Presidential AIDS Advisory Panel convened by [[Thabo Mbeki]] in 2000.<ref>{{cite news | url = http://www.villagevoice.com/news/0027,schoofs2,16283,1.html | title = Debating the Obvious: Inside the South African Government's Controversial AIDS Panel | first = Mark | last = Schoof | work = [[Village Voice]] | date = July 5–11, 2000 | accessdate = April 6, 2007 | archive-date = June 17, 2008 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080617232941/https://www.villagevoice.com/news/0027,schoofs2,16283,1.html | url-status = dead }}</ref> Bialy authored a scientific biography of [[Peter Duesberg]], a fellow AIDS denialist, in 2004.

==Education and early career==
Bialy graduated from [[Bard College]] in 1966 and was awarded a Ph.D. in [[molecular biology]] in 1970 by the [[University of California, Berkeley]]. He joined the journal ''[[Nature Biotechnology]]'' (part of the [[Nature Publishing Group|''Nature'' family of publications]]) as its scientific editor in 1984,<ref>''[[Nature Biotechnology]]'' '''2''', p. 109 (01 Feb 1984).</ref> and edited its peer-reviewed content from 1984 to 1996. He has co-authored papers in [[molecular genetics]], including articles presenting evidence that [[phage]] [[gene]]s can subvert [[host (biology)|host]] functions.<ref name="Lindahl">{{cite journal | doi=10.1073/pnas.66.3.587 |vauthors=Lindahl G, Sironi G, Bialy H, Calendar R | title=Bacteriophage Lambda; Abortive Infection of Bacteria Lysogenic for Phage P2 | journal=PNAS | year=1970 | pages=587–94 | volume=66 | issue=3 | pmid=4913204 | pmc=283090|bibcode=1970PNAS...66..587L |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name="Sironi">{{cite journal | doi=10.1016/0042-6822(71)90040-7 |vauthors=Sironi G, Bialy H, Lorenzon HA, Calendar R | title=Bacteriophage P2:interaction with phage lambda and with recombination-deficient bacteria | journal=Virology | year=1971 | pages=387–96 | volume=46 | issue=2 | pmid=4943192}}</ref> He has also written numerous editorials and commentaries on contemporary issues in biotechnology in Nature Biotechnology and other journals.<ref name="Curriculum Vitae">Bialy, Harvey. [http://www.harveybialy.org/wp-content/uploads/2009/11/cv.pdf Curriculum Vitae] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110726142203/http://www.harveybialy.org/wp-content/uploads/2009/11/cv.pdf |date=2011-07-26 }}. Accessed 16 November 2009.</ref> In 2004, Bialy authored ''Oncogenes, Aneuploidy, and AIDS'' ({{ISBN|1556435312}}), a book about the scientific life of fellow molecular biologist and AIDS denialist [[Peter Duesberg]], with special emphasis on Duesberg's version of the [[aneuploidy]] theory of cancer, on Duesberg's refusal to accept HIV as the cause of AIDS, and on the politics of modern science.

==Later career==
Bialy's resume indicated that he was the co-recipient of a grant from the Charles Merill Trust to study [[antibiotic resistance|antibiotic resistant]] pathogens in Nigeria in 1978. He received a [[World Health Organization]] grant to study the [[epidemiology]] and genetics of antibiotic resistant enteric pathogens in Nigeria in 1982. He worked as a visiting researcher or research fellow at several universities in the United States and Africa throughout the 1980s and 1990s. He was advisor to the Center for Biotechnology and Genetic Engineering in Havana, Cuba from 1986 to 1996.<ref name="Curriculum Vitae"/>

Bialy's CV also indicates that he was a resident scholar of the IBT at UNAM in [[Cuernavaca]] between 1996 and 2006,<ref name="Curriculum Vitae"/> where he also founded and directed the Virtual Library of Biotechnology for the Americas.<ref>[http://biblioteca.ibt.unam.mx/vcba/index.php Virtual Library of Biotechnology for the Americas] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110715224725/http://biblioteca.ibt.unam.mx/vcba/index.php |date=2011-07-15 }} homepage, accessed October 6, 2009.</ref>

In April 2006, [[Ordo Templi Orientis]] formed the International OTO Cabinet, an advisory, non-voting panel made up of both OTO Initiates and Non-Initiates. Along with [[David Tibet]], Bialy was named among the initial non-member appointments.<ref>[http://www.oto.org/news0806.html OTO International Cabinet appointments] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120222142733/http://www.oto.org/news0806.html |date=2012-02-22 }}. Published August 31, 2006. Last accessed June 2012.</ref>

==Artistic life==
He was also a poet<ref>Lopez, Richard. [http://jacketmagazine.com/25/lopez-beck.html "Unprotected Text: Tom Beckett in Conversation with Richard Lopez"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090925061937/http://jacketmagazine.com/25/lopez-beck.html |date=2009-09-25 }}, ''Jacket Magazine'', Issue 25, February 2004.</ref> and artist.<ref>[http://www.harveybialy.org Bialy's website featuring his artwork] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100818142240/http://www.harveybialy.org/ |date=2010-08-18 }}, accessed 16 November 2009.</ref> He published several books of poetry,<ref>[https://www.amazon.com/s/ref=nb_ss?url=search-alias%3Dstripbooks&field-keywords=harvey+bialy&x=0&y=0 Amazon.com search results for "Harvey Bialy"], accessed November 3, 2009.</ref> and in 1976, he received a fellowship in poetry from the [[National Endowment for the Arts]].<ref name="Curriculum Vitae"/> Since May 2007, he devoted his time to his art, of which an exposition "Telestics ... The Art of the Ordinary" was presented 23–31 August 2007 at the Catedral de Cuernavaca. The painter Rafael Cauduro admired Bialy's work and spoke in its praise for several minutes at the inauguration ceremony, which was also attended by the Minister of Culture of the [[Morelos|State of Morelos]].<ref>''El Sol de Cuernavaca'', 28 August 2007</ref> More recently, in February through April 2012, Bialy's work was featured at the Nalanda Gallery of [[Naropa University]].<ref>[http://www.93current.de/aggregator?page=157 "Harvey Bialy: To the Memory of Harry Smith"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304063532/http://www.93current.de/aggregator?page=157 |date=2016-03-04 }}, ''The 93 Current: A Thelemic Resource Page'', February 10, 2012</ref>
